newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korean Air shares plunge on crash news.
newsitem.headline: Korean Air shares plunge on crash news.

text.p: Shares of Korean Air Lines tumbled at the start of trading on Wednesday as investors dumped shares following news that a KAL jumbo jet had crashed in Guam, brokers said.
Korean Air, an affiliate of Hanjin Group, lost 800 won to 15,300, 10 minutes after the opening, they said.
"Investors are selling Korean Air stock thinking the accident would have a negative impact on the company," said a broker at LG Securities.
Brokers said the crash would hurt the airline's global image and could result in compensation payments and higher insurance costs.
Shares of other Hanjin Group units were also hit by the news.
Orient Fire Insurance fell 1,400 to 20,500 and Korean Air Terminal was down 300 won to 28,500.
A Korean Air jumbo jet carrying 231 passengers and 23 crew members crashed on the Pacific island of Guam on Wednesday.
Around 200 people died when the jumbo jet crashed and burst into flames after hitting an oil pipeline on the island.
